summary: This CSS file styles a fake terminal window that looks like macOS with a dark background, monospace font, traffic-light control buttons, and a copy button. It also includes animations for a blinking cursor and special handling to convert markdown headings (like # and ##) into bash comment syntax so they display as terminal commands rather than page headings.

explanations.8: This tells the CSS linter to ignore the rule against hardcoded hex color values, because this terminal component intentionally uses specific colors to look authentic rather than pulling from a design token system.
explanations.16: This allows the terminal to scroll horizontally if someone pastes an extremely long line of code that doesn't fit the width.
explanations.18: The terminal container uses `position: relative` so that child elements with `position: absolute` (like the copy button) position themselves inside it rather than somewhere higher up the page.
explanations.37: This prevents the icon and title from wrapping onto multiple lines — they stay together as a unit.
explanations.44: Even though the icon sits inside a flex container that might want to shrink it, `flex-shrink: 0` forces it to keep its full 16px width.
explanations.82: Without `pre-wrap`, long lines would just keep scrolling off to the right; this breaks them into multiple visual lines while keeping the whitespace intact (important for code formatting).
explanations.83: This ensures that even a single word or file path with no spaces can break mid-word if needed, so nothing overflows the container.
explanations.102: These two properties make the prompt symbol non-interactive: users can't select it when copying, and clicking on it does nothing.
explanations.130: This references a CSS variable defined by Docusaurus (the documentation framework) rather than a hardcoded value, keeping the button's border-radius consistent with the rest of the site.
explanations.138: This also uses a Docusaurus variable for the button color instead of hardcoding it, so the button automatically adapts to light/dark themes.
explanations.147: The copy button starts invisible (`opacity: 0`), but as soon as the user hovers over the terminal container, it becomes visible (`opacity: 1`).
explanations.164: This hidden clone element sits behind the animations to hold the terminal's final height steady during the typewriter animation, preventing the container from jumping around.
explanations.174: The overlay inherits the padding from its parent (the terminal body) so that animated text lines up pixel-perfectly with the static content underneath.
explanations.195: The cursor blinks by switching between fully visible and invisible every half-second, giving it that classic typewriter effect.
explanations.201: Because the content is written in markdown format, headings like `# comment` get converted to `<h1>` tags by the markdown parser. This selector resets all heading styles so they look like normal terminal text instead of large chapter headings.
